cognate: ON vera (pret. váru) = Goth. wisan, Gk ἄεσα/ἰαύω, Skt vas- < *h₂wes- 'spend the night, stay'; ON nátt = Gk νύξ < *nókʷt-
drift_or_renewal: ON vera has generalized to the copula, keeping the 'stay over' sense only in this construction; Skt renews the noun (rātri for nákt-); Greek keeps the verb specialized to night
shared_syntax: *h₂wes- verb + 'night' as accusative of duration (ON um nóttina / eina nótt), subject = travellers or guests, often with a place adverb (þar, ἐπ̓ ἠπείρου, gṛhe)
context: travellers take lodging and stay the night before going on (ON: Emund at Uppsala, then to the king next day); Od.: the ambushers never spent the night on land; AVŚ 15.13: the guest spends one night in a house
note: The root's sense 'spend the night' (LIV) is from memory. The Greek and Indic legs are strong; the Norse one is weak, because vera is the everyday copula and 'were there for the night' could arise anywhere. I claim it only as the root's old collocation with night surviving under the copula.

near_miss.lead: gift of a weapon: gaf mér brand ~ δώσω ὀξὺν ἄκοντα
near_miss.why_not: gefa and δίδωμι are not cognate and neither are brandr and ἄκων; giving a weapon is generic

near_miss.lead: heyra orð ... til eyrna (*h₂ḱh₂ows- with *h₂ows-, figura etymologica) ~ ἀκούσαντες λόγους
near_miss.why_not: the Greek partner has only 'hear' and no 'ear'; hearing words is generic

near_miss.lead: lagðe hǫfoð sitt i kne Jarli (submission gesture with the knee) ~ Homeric supplication at the knees (γούνων)
near_miss.why_not: the Greek partner is unrelated (the Herms); Norse puts the head in the lap rather than clasping the knees, which is a different gesture and not shared wording

near_miss.lead: polyptoton maðr manne 'man to man' (passing word on)
near_miss.why_not: there is no partner match; the 'man to man' polyptoton is widespread and generic

near_miss.lead: fœtr ... gengit (feet + walk) ~ padbhiḥ ... gacchataḥ; also fornar brautir 'old paths' ~ Ved. pathíbhiḥ pūrvyébhiḥ
near_miss.why_not: feet + go is generic; for 'old paths' the noun is not cognate and forn ~ pūrvya/purāṇa is only loosely related; the AVŚ partner lacks it

near_miss.lead: merism nótt ok dag / dag ok nótt ~ καὶ ἡμέρης καὶ νυκτός (nátt = νύξ; dagr renews ἡμέρα)
near_miss.why_not: 'day and night' is a near-universal merism; ON uses both orders, Greek has day first, and the MBh partners lack it

near_miss.lead: svaf hann þar um nóttina (*swep- + night acc.) ~ ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον
near_miss.why_not: the Greek is the reverse ('sleepless nights spent'); 'slept the night' is generic (see the *h₂wes- + night claim on BS-9b59e)

near_miss.lead: fell til fota konungi (fall at the feet, fótr = pād) ~ Skt pādayoḥ papāta
near_miss.why_not: the partners lack it; falla and pat are not cognate; falling at someone's feet is a universal gesture

near_miss.lead: kinship móðir mín er systir hans ~ OIr co siair do máthar 'to your mother's sister' (*méh₂tēr, *swésōr)
near_miss.why_not: the kin relations differ (mother's brother vs mother's sister) and the wording is compositional; it is not a fixed phrase

near_miss.lead: binda sætt (bind a settlement) ~ badhnantaḥ setuṃ (bind a causeway); cf. Hitt. išḫiul 'treaty' < *sh₂ey- 'bind'
near_miss.why_not: the Skt is a literal bridge-building with no treaty sense; the metaphor of binding a peace is widespread

error.correct_reading: óttask, medio-passive verb 'to fear' (þurpti ekki ... óttaz); not ótta 'pre-dawn'; the mapping to *nókʷt- is therefore wrong
vísu, acc. of fem. vísa 'stanza' (orti vísu)
personal name Sveinn (the would-be assassin), not the common noun
error.evidence: addressed by the king: hvat er nú Sveinn
